title: Ship a Chart Nobody Judges You For

sections.title: Kill the Gray Background
sections.prompt: Load titanic dataset with sns.load_dataset('titanic'). Plot df['fare'].hist() with zero styling — screenshot it. Then run sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid', palette='muted', font_scale=1.2) plus the rcParams block (dpi 150, figsize 10x6, spines off) and replot same histogram. Put both side by side, note 3 differences you see.

sections.title: Distribution Skew Check
sections.prompt: Run sns.histplot with kde=True on both df['age'] and df['fare'] side by side (subplots). Write one sentence on what the fare skew (most under £50, some over £500) means for using fare as raw model input vs log-transformed.

sections.title: Encode a Third Variable
sections.prompt: Build the age-vs-fare scatterplot with hue='survived' exact color mapping from tutorial ({0:'salmon',1:'steelblue'}). Then swap hue to 'pclass' instead. Compare which hue choice reveals a clearer pattern and explain why in 2 sentences.

sections.title: Read the Confidence Interval
sections.prompt: Reproduce sns.barplot(x='pclass', y='survived', errorbar='ci'). Note the survival rate and CI width for each class. Then rerun grouped by 'sex' instead of 'pclass' — does the CI get tighter or wider, and what does that tell you about sample size per group?

sections.title: Correlation Heatmap Audit
sections.prompt: Generate the sns.heatmap on numeric_cols.corr() with annot=True, cmap='coolwarm', center=0. Identify the strongest positive and strongest negative correlation pair (excluding self-correlations) and write what each pair implies about the Titanic data.

cta: Post your before/after chart screenshot (default matplotlib vs styled) and tag the correlation pair you found strongest — I'll reply with what I'd check next.
